items.title: Nonzero Temperley–Lieb cell forms give all simple heads

references.title: Andrew Mathas, Hecke algebras and Schur algebras of the symmetric group, complete prepublication manuscript (1998; expanded published edition: AMS University Lecture Series 15, 1999)
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2, printed pp. 11–16, Theorem 2.13 and its proof: nonzero cell-form quotients classify the simple modules of a finite-dimensional cellular algebra. The local statement follows the corrected condition that the form is not identically zero; it does not assert a zero form means the underlying module has zero head.

references.title: David Ridout and Yvan Saint-Aubin, Standard Modules, Induction and the Structure of the Temperley-Lieb Algebra
references.locator: §3, PDF pp. 14–15: the special zero-loop, zero-defect standard module and warning that the zero form quotient does not decide its actual head.
